$comment: The one place the loop's runner-observability patterns live.
Two languages read this file: `ralph/runner-failure.ts`, which classifies a
finished stage and writes the durable record, and `ralph/delegate-render.py`,
which is the only thing standing between a harness's event stream and a log
an operator reads. Both have to redact the same values and recognise the same
denials, and a second copy of either list is how a redactor comes to strip a
token in one place and print it in the other.
Every pattern here must therefore parse as BOTH a JavaScript and a Python
regular expression, and is applied case-insensitively by both readers: no
inline flags, no lookbehind, no named groups, no possessive quantifiers.
Keep them to the vocabulary the two engines share, and note the two places
they still differ, neither of which any pattern here may depend on:
`$` matches before a trailing newline in Python and only at the end in
JavaScript, so anchor on `$` for a whole NAME and never for a line; and
case-insensitivity is full Unicode folding in Python against simple folding
in JavaScript, so keep the patterns ASCII. `ralph/delegate-render.test.ts`
runs every entry below through both engines and fails on any disagreement.
$comment_evidence: How much of a matching line is kept as evidence, read by both readers so
the bound cannot be 300 in one and 400 in the other. A harness that fails
with a 400KB JSON body must not put all of it in a durable record.

$comment: A variable whose NAME matches any of these is treated as carrying a secret,
and its VALUE is struck from every line before it is printed or recorded.
Name-shaped rather than an explicit roster because the loop runs under
Doppler: a credential added there next month reaches the environment without
anyone touching this file, and a roster would silently not cover it.
`ralph.sh` withholds seven variables from the iteration outright. These
rules cover those names too — withholding is the first fence and this is the
second, because the executor and the read-only stages are not the only
things that can echo a value back.
Names that match a rule above but hold nothing secret. `_KEY$` catches
`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, which is the point, and `SORT_KEY`, which is
not; `AUTH` catches `SUPABASE_AUTH_URL`. Redacting a non-secret is not
harmless here — the value is often the very identifier an operator needs
to read the failure. `except` names the ones that ARE secret after all:
the database URLs, and the RALPH_BUILDKITE_* tokens a role declares as
its named secrets (`roles.ts`) — RALPH_ names, but credentials. Every
name in a role descriptor's `secrets.named` belongs here;
`observe.test.ts` fails if one is missing, because a credential the
redactor does not know by name is struck only if its SHAPE is listed.
Secret SHAPES, for the credentials that never passed through this process's
environment at all — the executor's own OpenCode token, a key a model read
out of a file, a `Bearer` header quoted back in an API error body. The
environment sweep cannot see any of those.
How a stage failed, in the kinds an operator acts on differently, ordered
MOST ACTIONABLE FIRST — the order is the precedence, so a run that both
timed out and hit a denial is reported as the denial. A missing grant is a
one-line repair; a timeout on top of it is a consequence.
These are matched against a harness's ERROR output only — a tool result
that failed, a diagnostic line, a non-zero stage's stderr. Never against
assistant prose: a review that says 'this code path is permission denied'
is a working review, and classifying it as a denial would make every
careful security report look like a broken runner.
Nor against a TOOL's output — what a command the model ran printed — except
for the kinds in `toolOutputKinds`. A rail refusal comes back inside a failed
command's output and nowhere else; a credential or provider failure is
reported on the harness's own channel (its stderr, a codex `error` or
`turn.failed` event, Claude's `permission_denials`). On 2026-09-23 a failing
test's 'Internal server error' and a source comment about 'an unauthorized
request' were recorded as api-error and authentication, and paged the operator
about a credential that was fine. Both readers label each signal with the
channel it came from (`source`: runner | tool).
$comment_benignLines: Runner lines that match a kind's pattern but are background chatter, not
the stage failing: neither reader raises a signal for a line matching one
of these. On 2026-09-29 a codex stage that exited 0 was recorded as a
stage timeout because codex logged that its model-list refresh timed out.

kinds.summary: the runner asked to do something its rails refuse
patterns: permission to use .* has been denied

kinds.summary: the runner has no usable credential
patterns: could not run under the (executor|stage)'s cleared environment

kinds.summary: the Claude subscription's usage limit is spent until it resets
$comment: Ahead of api-error because the repair differs: nothing is broken, the
loop has to wait for the window to reset. On 2026-10-21 thirteen loops
stopped on a five_hour rejection that the dashboard called an api-error,
and the reset time was only in the iteration log.
